Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 113, verses 1–5:

It is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

{1} That is: {Say}, seeking refuge: {I seek refuge}; i.e., I take refuge, seek shelter, and hold fast {in the Lord of the daybreak}; i.e., the Cleaver of the grain and the date-stone, and the Cleaver of the dawns.

{2} {From the evil of what He has created}: This includes everything Allah has created of humankind, jinn, and animals; so one seeks refuge in its Creator from the evil that is in them.

{3} Then He singled out what He had generalized, saying: {And from the evil of the darkness when it settles}; i.e., from the evil that occurs at night when it envelops people, and in which many evil spirits and harmful creatures spread.

{4} {And from the evil of the blowers in knots}; i.e., and from the evil of the sorceresses who seek help for their magic by blowing into the knots they tie for sorcery.

{5} {And from the evil of an envier when he envies}: The envier is the one who loves the removal of a blessing from the one envied, and so strives for its removal by whatever means he is able. Hence there was need to seek refuge in Allah from his evil and to nullify his scheming. The evil eye is included among the envier, for the evil eye does not proceed except from an envier who is evil in nature and wicked in soul.

This surah contains seeking refuge from all kinds of evils, generally and specifically, and it indicates that sorcery has a real existence, whose harm is to be feared, and one seeks refuge in Allah from it and from its practitioners.
